title: Conjugacy alone does not classify braid closures
statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The braids $\sigma_1\in B_2$ and $\sigma_2\in B_3$ have equivalent closures (both the unknot) but are not conjugate to each other, since conjugacy preserves the braid group and $B_2\ne B_3$. Hence conjugation alone, with the number of strands fixed, does not classify braid closures; at least one stabilization or destabilization is genuinely necessary.
strategy: Start with the one-strand trivial braid e, whose closure is a round unknot. Its positive stabilization is sigma_1 in B_2, whose closure is the unknot by ex-a-markov-stabilization-preserves-the-unknot-closure. Stabilize sigma_1 once more, adding the third strand on the right: the resulting braid is sigma_1 sigma_2 in B_3. The closure-preservation lemma gives an oriented ambient isotopy from its closure to that of sigma_1 (the added kink is unwound by the local R1 isotopy), hence both closures are unknots. AC implies the countable-choice hypothesis of that lemma via thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice. As a consistency check, sigma_1 in B_2 has the single permutation cycle (12), and sigma_1 sigma_2 in B_3 has a three-cycle, so both closures have one component; sigma_2 alone in B_3 has a fixed first strand and two components, which is why it was not the intended example. In the disjoint-union convention of def-markov-conjugation-and-stabilization-moves, conjugation stays within B_n and cannot change strand number, so no sequence of conjugations relates this B_2 braid to the B_3 braid. They are instead related by exactly one positive stabilization, illustrating the indispensable strand-changing Markov move. The statement retains AC because it cites the AC-stated Markov classification; the local kink isotopy itself is explicit.

references.title: Birman and Brendle, Braids: A Survey, Handbook of Knot Theory chapter, author manuscript; section 2 (printed pp. 12-26) and Figures 3-12
